title: Minimum deposit ignores Solana account storage overhead
description: MIN_DEPOSIT_LAMPORTS is meant to make the deposit receipt on Eclipse rent-exempt, but the rent calculation omits Solana's 128-byte ACCOUNT_STORAGE_OVERHEAD. The minimum deposit can be below the rent-exempt balance, so deposits may not be rent-exempt.

title: PDA bump is passed as an instruction argument
description: deposit and withdraw take the bump for the deposit_receipt and withdrawal_receipt PDAs as a user-supplied argument and store it, instead of using the canonical bump Anchor derives from the account context. A wrong bump can be recorded for the receipt accounts.

title: MessageSent emits the Ethereum chain id as the destination
description: sendMessage emits MessageSent with encodeChainId($.ethereumChainId) as the destination chain id. Messages go to Eclipse, so off-chain consumers that route on this field see the wrong chain; it should be the Eclipse chain id.

title: Outbox message logs can be truncated
description: log_outbox_message emits the encoded WithdrawalMessageSent with msg!. Solana truncates program logs beyond 10 KB, so large messages lose event data; CPI events avoid the limit.

title: 64-bit outbound nonce can collide
description: sendMessage takes a uint64 nonce from generateRandomNonce and stores it in sendNonces without checking whether it was already used. A 64-bit random nonce makes collisions plausible at high volume; use a wider nonce and reject reuse.

title: addressArrayInitialized accepts an empty array
description: addressArrayInitialized checks every element is non-zero but never checks that the array is non-empty, so an empty array passes validation.

title: Bridge funds are custodied by the relayer account
description: The relayer account holds custody of all bridged funds on the Solana side. If that key is compromised every bridged fund is lost; a program-derived account governed by program logic would remove that single point of failure.

title: Implementation contracts can be initialized directly
description: The upgradeable implementations of EtherBridge, Treasury, and Mailbox do not call _disableInitializers in a constructor, so anyone can call initialize on the implementation address, become its owner, and potentially brick it.

title: invoke_signed used where invoke suffices
description: deposit and withdraw call invoke_signed even though no signer seeds are needed; plain invoke is sufficient.

title: Oversized account allocations
description: Configuration and WithdrawalReceipt allocate 1024 bytes each, although they need about 11 and 57 bytes. The excess wastes rent.
